AUTHORIZATION_CODE.label: Authorization Code
AUTHORIZATION_CODE.description: Two-step browser-based authentication. The user authenticates first, then grants consent to the requested scopes

REFRESH_TOKEN.label: Refresh Token
REFRESH_TOKEN.description: Used when the access_token has expired but the user should not re-authenticate

CLIENT_CREDENTIALS.label: Client Credentials
CLIENT_CREDENTIALS.description: The client obtains a token on its own behalf rather than on behalf of a user. Used for service-to-service interaction without binding to a specific logged-in user

JWT_BEARER.label: JWT Bearer
JWT_BEARER.description: Used when the client presents a ready-made JWT issued by a trusted external party

DEVICE_CODE.label: Device Code
DEVICE_CODE.description: Used when a device has no browser and/or keyboard (Smart TVs, consoles, IoT devices). The user confirms sign-in from another device

TOKEN_EXCHANGE.label: Token Exchange
TOKEN_EXCHANGE.description: Used for scenarios like 'microservice A' received a user token and wants to exchange it for a token with reduced privileges to call 'microservice B'

CLIENT_SECRET_BASIC.label: Client Secret Basic
CLIENT_SECRET_BASIC.description: The most common method — HTTP Basic Auth. Data (client_id, client_secret) is sent in the Authorization header (Authorization: Basic base64(client_id:client_secret))

CLIENT_SECRET_POST.label: Client Secret POST
CLIENT_SECRET_POST.description: Data (client_id, client_secret) is sent in the form body

CLIENT_SECRET_JWT.label: Client Secret JWT
CLIENT_SECRET_JWT.description: The client does not send the secret directly but signs a JWT assertion with this secret (symmetric HMAC).

PRIVATE_KEY_JWT.label: Private Key JWT
PRIVATE_KEY_JWT.description: Same as 'Client Secret JWT' but with asymmetric cryptography — the client signs the JWT with its private key, and the SSO server verifies it with the public key

NONE.label: None
NONE.description: For clients that physically cannot keep a secret: SPAs without a backend, mobile applications. In this case, security is ensured via PKCE

TLS_CLIENT_AUTH.label: PKI-based mTLS
TLS_CLIENT_AUTH.description: The client presents a TLS certificate issued by a trusted certificate authority (CA). The server verifies the certificate trust chain and compares one of its attributes with a pre-stored value for this client

SELF_SIGNED_TLS_CLIENT_AUTH.label: Self-signed certificates
SELF_SIGNED_TLS_CLIENT_AUTH.description: The difference from PKI-based mTLS is one thing: the client certificate does not have to be issued by a trusted CA — self-signed is allowed. Instead of verifying the trust chain, the server compares the certificate itself (more precisely, its thumbprint) with the one pre-registered for the client — following the 'pinning' model (similar to certificate/public-key pinning)

oidcLogoutRedirectUri.label: URI for user logout (OIDC Logout Redirect URI)
